title: Automated proration rules and credit ledger for mid-cycle subscription downgrades
creator: Emily Park
description: Background: Enterprise customers are downgrading plans mid-billing-cycle (e.g., from Reserved Capacity to Pay-as-you-go) or applying contract changes that should trigger partial refunds/credits. Current billing flow requires manual ops intervention to calculate proration and to issue credits, which increases turnaround time and error rates. Goal: Design and ship a deterministic, auditable automation that calculates proration for mid-cycle subscription changes, posts credits to a customer-visible ledger, and integrates with the automated invoice runner to avoid duplicate charges.
goals: Define deterministic proration rules for the common contract types (monthly reserved, annual reserved with monthly invoice, payg add-ons)
Implement a ledger entry model that surfaces credits and reversals in invoices and the Console billing UI
Automate credit issuance for downgrades and failed overage disputes with a clear audit trail
Reduce ops manual tickets related to mid-cycle adjustments by 80% in Q2
out_of_scope: One-off bespoke enterprise legal credit requests that require CFO sign-off
acceptance_criteria: Proration calculator covers 3 contract templates and matches sample calculations in the spec
Credit ledger entries are visible in Console (token-level breakdown not required) and attached to the next generated invoice
Automated credit postings include a reason code, original invoice reference, and traceable request id
System generates a report of adjustments for the operations team and reduces manual ticket volume per metric
technical_notes: Front-end: Console changes to billing UI to show 'Pending credits' and ledger rows
Backend: New billing-service endpoint POST /adjustments that validates contract terms and creates ledger entries
Data model: Add AdjustmentRecord with fields (referenceId, reasonCode, prorationFactor, amountCents, currency, createdBy, linkedInvoiceId) — sample export included in doc
Edge cases: prorate for plans with changing seat counts, monthly usage tiers, and committed credits
Fail-safes: If automated calc fails validation, create ops-review task and do not modify invoice
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect proration for unusual enterprise add-ons — Mitigation: start with 3 templates and require manual review toggle for custom contracts
Risk: Duplicate credits if invoice runner and manual ops both process same event — Mitigation: idempotency keys and reconciliation report
Risk: Customer confusion when credits appear after invoice generation — Mitigation: email notification and Console visibility labeled with clear reason codes
